newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS heating oil falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS heating oil falls on profit-taking.

text.p: Prices for U.S. heating oil futures fell overnight Thursday, as profit-taking undercut the market's daytime rally, traders said.
Volume was light to moderate on ACCESS, the overnight futures market run by NYMEX.
"It could be somebody doing some profit-taking. There's nothing in the news to support it going down," traders said, referring to the fall in heating oil.
Prices for the fuel jumped 1.75 cents a gallon during the day, as temperatatures fell in the U.S. Northwest, the world's largest consumer of "heat."
After-hours, NYMEX May heating oil traded at 54.60 cents, a 0.26-cent loss from the daytime settle. A light 75 lots traded in May, with 208 contracts exchanged overall.
Crude oil for May delivery was nearly unchanged on ACCESS, rising two cents a gallon to $19.59 a barrel. Over 652 lots traded, a moderate volume, according to traders.
Unleaded gasoline for May delivery changed hands at 61.15 cents gallon, a slight gain of 0.08 cents a gallon from the settle as 104 lots traded in the nearby month and 210 changed hands in total.
